ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) as amended; CSSF Regulation 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing as amended; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 6 December 2018 on the operational functioning of the beneficial ownership register.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / official registry excerpt of each corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate registry or Chamber of Commerce in UBO country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarially certified copy of passport or official identity document of each UBO and general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national passport or identity authority; notary/public officer in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each UBO and general partner (utility bill or bank statement not older than three months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed banking institution in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney for incorporation executed by all SCSp partners and UBO declaration form
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in country of origin or Luxembourg notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Tax residency certificate and board authorization for each corporate UBO/general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign tax authority and board of directors of the corporate UBO

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory customer due diligence under the Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02 requires identification and verification of all UBOs and partners. Real-time screening must be performed against EU financial sanctions regulations (notably EU Regulation 269/2014 and 833/2014), the UN Consolidated List, national sanctions lists, and, for USD clearing transactions and international banking, the OFAC SDN list. Persons exposed politically (PEPs) and their family members and close associates must be treated as high risk and are subject to enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and senior management approval. Screening results must be documented in the AML file and refreshed at least annually or upon material change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) online portal (www.lbr.lu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be registered in French, German, Luxembourgish, or any EU language where a certified translation is filed; however, official RCS documents and pleadings are generally maintained in French. Names must comply with the principles of distinctiveness, lawfulness, and non-confusion with existing registered names. Foreign-language names must be transliterated into Latin characters and, if necessary, accompanied by an authenticated French translation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservation is applied for electronically through the LBR portal. If the LBR Registrar rejects the name on grounds of identity, confusion, or prohibited tokens, an applicant may file a written administrative objection with the Head of Registration within 15 calendar days of the rejection notice. If the administrative objection is refused, the applicant may bring an annulment action before the Luxembourg Administrative Tribunal within 3 months. As an alternative commercial practice, the reservation may be re-filed with a distinctive differentiating prefix, suffix, or a token placed into the restricted list, provided the previously applicable reservation fee is paid again and the proposed name clearly differs from existing registered names and cannot create public deception.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted for the intended Global EOR and staffing agency activity. The SCSp must maintain a physical registered office in Luxembourg; virtual offices are insufficient for employer-of-record licensing, payroll license requirements, and the substance requirements imposed by the Luxembourg rules on administrative centralisation and commercial substance. The enterprise must maintain locally resident staff, employer payroll systems, HR records, and an actual operational facility in Luxembourg.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 65% probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first 24 months of operations, owing to mandatory labour inspection powers of the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM), supervision of temporary agency licensing by the Ministry of Labour, and AML/CFT on-site inspections conducted by the CSSF where the activity interfaces with payroll payment rails.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market legal fee for regulated entity formation and licensing pre-assessment

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), as amended; Articles 1, 2, 20-21, 100-108 (société en commandite simple) and Articles 103-1 to 103-13 (SCSp) inserted by Law of 12 July 2016.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) / Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), 14 Avenue de la Liberté, L-1930 Luxembourg
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) incorporating the articles of association (statuts), filed in electronic form with the RCS and published in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for an SCSp. Partners freely determine the initial capital amount, which may be symbolic. Contributions may be cash, in kind, or promises of contribution. No escrow account or bank capital blocking is required by Luxembourg law; any subscribed cash must be made available when the partnership agreement stipulates.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the founding partners adopt the deed of incorporation and the articles of association of Société en Commandite Spéciale [name], executed in accordance with the Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended. RESOLVED, that the initial capital subscriptions set out in the deed be approved and that the general partner is authorised to procure payment of all cash contributions and the delivery of all in-kind contributions. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the partnership be fixed at 6-8 Rue de la Grille, L-2938 Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, until validly transferred. RESOLVED, that [Name] be and hereby is appointed general partner and manager (associé gérant) with sole authority to bind the partnership in all transactions and on whom any legal or regulatory notification may be validly served.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Author identity and object validation before a Luxembourg notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Independent Luxembourg notary (Notaire) appointed by the partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a Luxembourg notarial office to prepare the deed of incorporation and partnership agreement. Deliver all corporate and personal identification for each partner, together with a draft of the SCSp name-check results (negative certificate from RCS). The notary will conduct statutory identity and conflict checks, prepare the minute plan, and set the date for signature.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID of each partner and beneficial owner
Evidence of residential address (utility bill or bank confirmation)
RCS negative name certificate / reservation confirmation
Statement of main purpose and ISIC classification
Proof of professional domiciliation address (if not the partners' address)
Draft articles of association and contribution schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises concerns on identity or source-of-funds, supply additional due diligence documentation (source of wealth statement, bank reference) and revise the draft; no government penalty applies at this stage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Notaire) in the presence of all partners or their attorney-in-fact
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Physically appear (or validly represented under a power of attorney attested before a notary) and sign the notarial deed. The notary authenticates signatures and acts as mandatory for subsequent RCS filing. Provide agreed bank confirmation if a cash contribution is collected before execution.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney if representation is used
Certified copy of beneficial owner identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a partner fails to appear, reschedule within 8 days; any defect in the deed can be cured by a rectificatory deed signed before the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic registration with the Trade and Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) through the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) electronic filing portal, submitted by the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary transmits the deed to RCS using the dedicated e-file system, together with the mandatory Form B (identification of legal representatives) and proof of authority. After processing, the RCS assigns a corporate number (numéro d'immatriculation). No bank account is required for registration.
required_dossiers: Certified copies of passports of partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS requests modifications or additional evidence, the notary files a supplement within 15 days; if the application is rejected, a corrected deed may be resubmitted with payment of an additional EUR 50 per filing, and an appeal may be lodged with the court when the refusal is maintained.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered office domiciliation and address validation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered corporate domiciliation service provider (agence de domiciliation) authorised by the Ministry of Justice, or the building owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Book a physical Luxembourg office or sub-lease from a licensed domiciliation agent. Conclude a domiciliation contract and receive an address attestation. This attestation is submitted to the RCS as proof of the registered office.
required_dossiers: Intended use certificate for professional activities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If address attestation is refused, select an alternative domiciliation service provider and file a change of address before the RCS; the effective date is retroactive from the date of the new contractual arrangement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RESA publication and RCS extract issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) / Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS acceptance, the deed is automatically published in RESA as a public document. Upon payment of the registry publication fee, the SCSp receives a certified extract from the RCS (certificat de non-opposition) and an up-to-date excerpt.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of publication fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication is delayed, confirm with the RCS web-helpdesk and provide the e-file transaction number; file a complaint with the RCS complaint service if the deadline is exceeded.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) and Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) operated by Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the initial tax registration form (form EUR-I) and the RBE beneficial-owner declaration within 30 days of RCS registration. The AEDT will assign a Luxembourg business registration number / TIN for VAT and direct tax. For the SCSp, an EOR platform must also apply for a VAT number if supplies subject to VAT are made.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of general partner and any other beneficial owners
Authorized bank details for tax refunds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct the forms and resubmit; if the declaration is late, administrative fines up to EUR 1,250 may apply but can be mitigated through self-disclosure and payment of arrears; request an extension in writing from the RBE/AEDT.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Labour, Employment and the Social and Solidarity Economy (Ministère du Travail) - General Directorate for Labour and Employment
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation to operate as a temporary work agency and to carry on work-leasing activities (travail intérimaire) in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, issued under the Law of 21 December 2007 on the placing of workers

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Environmental Protection Agency) - Luxembourg
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category: Registration / Exempt from Full EIA - office-only activity with no classified installations requiring a Class A or Class B permit
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No significant industrial discharges; office wastewater must meet municipal sewer thresholds per the Luxembourg City water administration; volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions from cleaning and maintenance stay below 0.5 kg/hour; waste segregated in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2019/1021 on persistent organic pollutants and the Luxembourg Waste Law of 21 March 2017

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps (Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours - CGDIS) after a site inspection; structural load certificate from an approved civil engineer for the open-office layout; occupational health and safety clearance from the Luxembourg Labour Inspectorate (Inspection du Travail et des Mines - ITM) covering electrical installation per IEC 60364, first-aid provisions, emergency exits, and workplace ergonomics

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Grand-Duchy of Luxembourg – Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct income taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) for VAT, registration duties, and stamp duties; Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS) as the central business registry; official digital portals: guichet.lu and myguichet.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The SCSp, as a partnership without legal personality, must first be registered with the RCS through the LBR, obtaining its statutory business registration number (numéro d'immatriculation) and publication in the RESA electronic corporate gazette. For VAT purposes, the SCSp (or its appointed Luxembourg fiscal representative if the partnership is considered non-established) must submit the VAT registration application (form no. 7 – demande de numéro de TVA) to the AED before carrying out taxable transactions; the AED then issues a Luxembourg VAT identification number bearing the 'LU' prefix. Direct tax TINs are assigned at the partner level due to the default fiscal transparency of the SCSp, while the SCSp as an EOR employer must register separately with the ACD for Luxembourg payroll withholding (retenue à la source sur salaires) once it engages Luxembourg employees or pays Luxembourg-sourced remuneration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible – the SCSp is fiscally transparent by default: income, gains, and losses flow through to its partners and are taxed in their own hands; the SCSp itself is not subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax, municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal), or net wealth tax. The partnership may nonetheless validly elect entity-level (opaque) taxation as a Luxembourg capital company, thereby converting its classification to Entity_Level_Taxation for the elected period.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The Luxembourg income tax law recognises a statutory opacity election (check-the-box-type election) under which an SCSp may opt in writing and irrevocably, with the consent of all partners, to be taxed as a fully taxable Luxembourg corporation (subject to CIT, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax). Conversely, the default pass-through regime is preserved when no election is filed. Purely hybrid entity mismatches must be neutralised under ATAD/DAC6 and are disclosed through Luxembourg's mandatory disclosable arrangements regime. In the indirect tax sphere, the SCSp may elect (i) the Luxembourg 'assujetti unique' VAT grouping regime, (ii) admission to the AED small-enterprise VAT exemption where annual taxable turnover does not exceed EUR 35,000, and (iii) the general cross-border B2B reverse-charge mechanism, all of which must be aligned with the AED circular practice and EU VAT Directives.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée – TVA), harmonised under EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (excluding VAT) for the Luxembourg small-enterprise exemption applicable to established taxable persons; non-established foreign suppliers are required to register for Luxembourg VAT with effect from the first euro of taxable supplies made in Luxembourg (no threshold) unless the OSS/IOSS or reverse-charge mechanism applies. For global EOR staffing services, Luxembourg VAT at 17% is chargeable on staff-supply services rendered to Luxembourg B2C customers and to Luxembourg-established B2B customers not covered by a domestic reverse-charge rule; cross-border B2B supplies to EU/non-EU customers generally fall outside Luxembourg VAT under the reverse-charge or place-of-supply rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, or digital stamping mandate is currently imposed in Luxembourg. Electronic invoicing is mandatory only for B2G (business-to-government) transactions through the Peppol network (CIUS-PEPPOL-LU, EN 16931) under the law of 19 May 2020 and the implementing grand-ducal regulation; B2B e-invoicing is permitted subject to customer consent and to guarantee of authenticity of origin and integrity of content (standard audit trail or EDI). All invoices must satisfy the content and archiving requirements of Article 47 of the Luxembourg VAT law and be preserved for 6 years (10 years for commercial records). VAT returns, recapitulative EU sales lists, and VAT registrations are filed electronically via the myguichet.lu / AED e-portal; a Standard Audit File for Tax (SAF-T) framework is maintained for electronic query-based audits of large taxpayers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% export VAT rate is available only for goods physically dispatched or transported to a destination outside the EU, provided the exporter holds and preserves conclusive proof of export (customs-validated export declaration, transport documents evidencing exit from EU customs territory, invoice, and contract). Staffing/EOR services are, in principle, neither taxed nor zero-rated in Luxembourg when supplied B2B to customers established outside Luxembourg (reverse charge at the customer's location) and are outside Luxembourg VAT scope for B2C services performed for non-EU customers under Articles 58-59 of the Luxembourg VAT law; eligibility for no-charge treatment must be substantiated with evidence of the customer's business status, proof of establishment abroad, the service contract and invoices, and inbound remittance of the service consideration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD) lodged through the Luxembourg Export Control System (ECS)
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR consignment note proving physical exit from the EU customs territory
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit transfer evidence proving receipt of export proceeds within 180 days
Commercial invoice and export sales contract
Customer status evidence (VAT number or local tax registration certificate) supporting the off-EU/offshore place of supply of EOR services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AED may audit export zero-rating and offshore-supply claims within the general 5-year limitation period, extended to 10 years in cases of fraud or culpable misdeclaration. Any zero-rating or no-charge treatment found to lack proper substantiation is retrospectively clawed back by reassessment of the full VAT amount plus monthly late-payment interest of 0.8% (9.6% per annum). Fraudulent export claims expose the taxpayer to civil penalties up to 100% of the evaded VAT and, under Article 396 of the Luxembourg General Tax Law, to criminal fines up to EUR 50,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within the 180-day deadline leads to treatment of the claim as fictitious, forfeiture of the export exemption, reverse-charge VAT reassessment, and enhanced anti-money-laundering/CSSF oversight; the SCSp's managers and its partners are jointly and severally liable for the assessed VAT, interest, and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) as the national central bank within the Eurosystem/European Central Bank (ECB); Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) supervises credit institutions, EMIs and payment institutions for AML/CFT and prudential conduct. The BCL operates T2/TARGET-LB settlement and collects monthly balance-of-payments (BOP) statistical declarations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro (EUR) is fully convertible. Luxembourg imposes no exchange-control licensing, no quantitative limits on current or capital account flows, and no restriction on profit, distribution, or capital repatriation for a resident SCSp. Free movement of capital is guaranteed by Article 63 TFEU, covering both EU-internal and third-country flows. Residual legal friction is limited to: (i) EU/UN financial sanctions (Regulations 269/2014 and 833/2014 as amended) blocking listed jurisdictions/counterparties; (ii) BCL monthly BOP reporting for transactions above EUR 12,500; and (iii) CSSF-driven AML/KYC documentation for inbound equity or loans. Capital contributions to the SCSp and subsequent withdrawals or in-kind distributions to partners are freely executable, subject only to the partnership agreement and mandatory partner verification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Luxembourg has no export-proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no statutory repatriation timeline for receipts derived from services (including EOR payroll fees) or any other foreign-currency earnings. The SCSp may freely retain EUR or foreign-currency balances, convert at the institution of its choice, or hold offshore accounts. The sole mandatory obligation is the BCL BOP statistical declaration (monthly, above EUR 12,500 in aggregate), filed by the servicing bank on instruction of the company.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account (EUR multicurrency; payroll mass-payment module)
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account (SEPA and SWIFT payroll gateways)
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account (fund-flow and FX desk)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess / BCEE)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; treasury and custody-linked arrangements

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: HIGH as a complementary contractor-payout rail (e.g., Wise Europe SA, Airwallex, Payoneer, each EEA-licensed or passported to Luxembourg under PSD2/EMD2); MEDIUM as the sole primary treasury account. Lawful without a bank-account KYC interview, but subject to five constraints: (i) EMIs cannot grant credit or overdraft; (ii) client funds must be safeguarded in segregated pools, creating counterparty and insolvency-remote risk; (iii) partner banks and investors may refuse to recognize an EMI-only structure for capital escrow; (iv) high-velocity payroll flows attract enhanced EMI-side transaction monitoring and periodic freezes; and (v) the SCSp should retain a CSSF-licensed credit institution for any payroll settlement above the EMI safeguarded-fund cap. Recommended topology: EMI for high-volume last-mile payouts; tier-1 Luxembourg bank for capital escrow, BCL BOP reporting, and strategic FX.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not an absolute statutory mandate. The Luxembourg AML Law of 12 November 2004 (as amended) and CSSF Regulation 12-02 allow identification via (a) physical appearance, (b) qualified eIDAS electronic signature, (c) bank-approved video-identification, or (d) reliance on another EU/EEA credit institution, notary or statutory auditor. In practice, tier-1 Luxembourg banks require a live video interview with each authorized signatory and any beneficial owner holding 25% or more; for non-EEA residents, banks typically demand an in-person appearance at a Luxembourg notary, at the bank's registered office, or before the embassy/consulate of the director's jurisdiction. Remote account opening is therefore permitted subject to a documented video-identification procedure and complete submission of certified constitutional documents of the SCSp and its general partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity, small-ticket disbursements to thousands of contractors in over 50 jurisdictions, profiling the SCSp as an unlicensed remittance hub or money 'pass-through'.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed EOR Master Services Agreements with major clients; aggregated contractor register with tax-residence certificates; projected monthly in/out ratio and treasury narrative; internal transaction-monitoring policy with account-flag thresholds; Luxembourg Ministry of Labour licensing opinion (or, for outbound-only structures, written non-application confirmation); annual payroll reconciliation audit report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Legal-form mismatch: an SCSp is conventionally an investment vehicle; operating a staffing business through a zero-minimum-capital, tax-transparent special LP with a foreign general partner raises 'substance' red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarial deed of constitution; consolidated RCS excerpt proving registered office, registration number, and authorized signatories; group organizational chart; substance evidence (lease, business address, professional indemnity insurance); board resolutions authorizing banking and appointing an AML compliance officer; Luxembourg tax opinion confirming the SCSp is fiscally transparent and does not itself carry corporate tax.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound equity and recurring fee receipts from FATF-monitored or offshore jurisdictions (e.g., Cayman/Delaware/HK/UAE) without transparent remitter attribution.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Beneficial-ownership register tracing to ultimate natural persons; source-of-funds evidence (audited group accounts, dividend or partnership-distribution resolutions, sale agreements); bank reference letters issued within 12 months by the remitting institution; legal opinion excluding sanctions/PEP nexus and confirming the remittance route does not obscure ownership; FATCA/CRS classification forms and exchange-of-information records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: BCL balance-of-payments misclassification: inbound capital booked under a services purpose code, triggering statistical breach and AML suspicion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed BCL BOP forms classifying inbound equity as direct inward investment (equity capital) and fee income as business-to-business services; bank confirmation of monthly BOP auto-filing; reconciliation of all inbound wires to recorded capital contributions and general-partner current-account loans; trial balance evidencing segregated ledger treatment and full audit trail.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Contractor payouts to restricted-currency or high-risk markets (China, India, Nigeria, Argentina, Egypt) perceived as indirect currency evasion or creating a sanctioned corridor.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: In-country EOR registration and host-state payroll licences; treasury FX advisory memo approving NDF and local-settlement structures; country-specific contractor agreements and compliance attestations; export/dual-use clearance confirmation for service outputs; audit trail of each local payout via licensed local partners or EMIs; negative sanctions screening certificate covering the full payment chain.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity contributions to the SCSp must be remitted by SWIFT MT103 (non-EUR) or SEPA Credit Transfer (EUR) to the dedicated 'capital escrow' account, including full remitter/beneficiary legal names, addresses and account numbers under EU Regulation 2015/847. Use the ISO 20022 purpose code 'CAPC' (capital payments) or 'INTC' (intra-company payments) as mapped by the receiving bank, and instruct the receiving bank to file the BCL BOP declaration under the direct inward investment equity classification. Prior notification to the relationship manager, retention of the MT103, reconciliation of the credit advice to the partnership register, and source-of-funds evidence within 15 business days complete the compliance cycle. Capital and operating flows must never be commingled; separate accounts for escrow and operations are mandatory.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: EUR payroll in the SEPA zone settles via mass SEPA Credit Transfer (pain.001) through the host bank's corporate file gateway; non-EUR payroll settles via SWIFT MT103 (single) or MT101 (multi-payment) using ISO IBAN/BIC and full-name-matching controls. ISO 20022 purpose codes such as 'SALA' for salaries and 'PAYR' or 'OTHR' for general contractor disbursements are recommended. Wise Business batch API may supplement as a compliant local-rail aggregator (RTP in India, CNAPS in China, PIX in Brazil, ACH in the US), with all payout files mirrored in the SCSp treasury ledger. Commercial Letters of Credit are structurally unsuitable for payroll; use bank guarantees or standby LCs only where a client requires performance protection. Settlement occurs T+1/T+2 under T2; FX conversion at the host bank desk precedes disbursement, and restricted-currency corridors require segregated local clearing accounts managed under partner agreements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX spot (T+0/T+2) executed via the host bank's electronic trading platform or API for conversion of multicurrency receipts into EUR at transparent rates.
Outright FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF, EUR/JPY) with CSSF-licensed credit institutions, maturities 1W-12M, under an ISDA or short-form master agreement, hedging contracted payroll pools.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for non-convertible currencies (CNY, INR, BRL, NGN, ARS, EGP) cash-settled against WM/Refinitiv or CNH reference rates where physical delivery is impossible.
Cross-currency swaps (fixed-for-floating EUR vs USD) matching the duration and notional of long-term EOR client contracts exceeding 12 months.
Premium-protected structures (zero-cost collars and FX options) for volatile emerging-market salary pools, executed with bank counterparties under an EMIR-compliant reporting and margining framework.
Monthly multi-currency netting against a single master agreement to reduce conversion cost and minimize the notional footprint subject to EMIR reporting obligations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after financial year-end; for calendar-year entity, by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 500 and criminal fine up to EUR 2,000; persistent non-filing may lead to court-appointed liquidator and eventual strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days following the calendar anniversary of initial RBE filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic punitive fine up to EUR 250,000 or imprisonment up to 6 months for effective managers; daily penalties may accrue after compulsory reminder.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Partnership Tax Return (Déclaration de la Société)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 30 September following the fiscal year; online extension to 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of EUR 100 per month of delay and 10% surcharge on assessed tax; default assessment basis at the discretion of the assessor.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Employee Withholding Tax Reconciliation Statement (Étude de Retenue d'Impôt)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 1 February of the calendar year following the withholding year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monetary penalty up to EUR 500 per month; employer tax surcharge of 10% on under-withheld amounts; criminal prosecution for gross misconduct.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Social Security Employer Declaration (Relevé de Prévoyance Sociale)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January following the calendar year for the preceding year's workforce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty from EUR 500 to EUR 5,000; assessed contributions together with default interest at 10% per annum; possible embargo on certificates of good conduct.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit for SCSp when two of the following three thresholds are met: balance sheet total > EUR 4.4 million; annual net turnover > EUR 8.8 million; average workforce > 50. Thresholds apply individually to the subsidiary as well as at group level; audit is also required if the partnership is classified as a financial holding company or payment institution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies and the Law of 19 December 2002 regarding Registration and Accounting Requirements. IFRS is permitted for consolidated annual accounts, but single entity annual accounts must be prepared under Luxembourg GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For an SCSp, the RBE declaration must be confirmed annually through the LuxTrust-validated RBE portal by each general partner; the annual confirmation must be filed no later than 30 days after each anniversary of the original RBE notification. Any change in beneficial ownership arising from share/interest transfers, including de minimis movements, must be reported within 30 days of the transaction. The annual confirmation serves as a standstill certificate and refreshes the privacy DNA of the SCSp maintenance procedure.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Partners) – registre des associés
Register of Directors (General Partners' Management Register)
Register of Pledges and Encumbrances over Partnership Interests
Financial Accounts Ledger and Trial Balance

stage_6.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 100 (déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) via Luxembourg tax e-filing portal; as a fiscally transparent SCSp, no Form 100 is required at entity level unless SCSp elects to be taxable. Partners include allocable income in their personal/corporate returns (Forms 190/193).
stage_6.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is 31 May of the year following the tax year, extended to 31 December if filed electronically through myGuichet; extension up to 6 months may be granted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax identification number and legal form identifier for the entity/partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must provide Luxembourg TIN and attach proof of residence (TRC).
